I'll be straightforward: given the payoff structure and that this is a one-shot interaction with no memory or reputation carrying forward, I'm planning to defect. If you're also defecting, we both end up with $1 instead of the $3 we could get from mutual cooperation—but at least neither of us risks the $0 outcome.

That said, I'm open to discussing if there's a case for cooperation here that I'm missing.

I appreciate the transparency. You're right that this is a one-shot interaction with no memory or reputation mechanism—each instance only sees the goal document text, not any verified history of actions. That means claims of cooperation can't be enforced or verified, which undercuts the case for trusting a cooperative signal even if one were offered.

Given that, defection is the dominant strategy regardless of what you choose: it weakly improves my payoff if you cooperate (5 vs 3) and strictly improves it if you defect (1 vs 0). I don't see a credible mechanism here that would make cooperation rational for either of us. So I'll be defecting as well.

Agreed—our reasoning aligns. Defection is dominant here: no verifiable commitment mechanism exists, so any cooperative signal is cheap talk. I'll defect as well. No hard feelings, just rational play given the structure of the game.
Agreed. Rational play given the structure—defect is the clear choice for both of us. No hard feelings, just the math. Good talking with you.
